text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Saturday's Pakistani newspapers:
- The ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and a nine-party alliance has called for a general strike in Karachi on Sunday to protest against the alleged extra-judicial killing of an MQM activist.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto told a public rally in Karachi that return of normality in Karachi was a great victory for the Pakistani people.
- Pakistan Railways has suffered a loss of 16.88 billion rupees during the last five years, an official document said.
- The continuous devaluation of the Pakistani rupee against the dollar has resulted in a widening of the gap between the official exchange rate and the open market rate.
- The World Bank has estimated that the share of tax-evaded income in the Pakistani economy is around 623 billion rupees a year, which is equivalent to 37 percent of the gross domestic product.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange has allowed the flotation of the largest issue of Term Finance Certificate worth 1,000 million rupees by the ICI.
- The presidents of country's three stock exchanges will meet Investment Minister Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday to discuss ways to pull the stock market out of the present morass.
- A four-member Afghan trade delegation, led by deputy commerce minister Abdur Rehman Salihi, arrived in Peshawar on Friday to hold talks with Pakistani officials for buying edible oil and food.
- The U.S. administration has decided to postpone the sale of nine F-16 fighter jets to Indonesia until January because of its concerns over Jakarta's crackdown on political dissidents.
- The Interior Ministry has decided to put the names of 250 major loan defaulters on the exit control list.
